findings.desc: lattice.config.json:150-157 label for red-b45a5-withdrawal-gates.mjs (now mandatory, no longer optional) states only "must keep EXCLUDING an item-level withdrawal authorized by a confirmed decision, and must keep biting on everything that is not withdrawn." That is the guards A1/A2/B1-B3 half. It omits the CHK-004 anti-bypass half (D1-D5: unbacked status=withdrawn with no/dangling/mismatched decisionRef, or decision=rejected/userConfirmed=false, must still be refused by both gates) entirely. The test file itself treats these as a THIRD, distinct clause -- its own GREEN report text (red-b45a5-withdrawal-gates.mjs tail) reads "both gates exclude the decision-backed withdrawn item, both still bite on everything that is not withdrawn, AND every unbacked withdrawal is still refused by both" -- three clauses, not two. A future reader who sees this guard start failing and consults only the config label will not learn that the failure could mean the withdrawal mechanism became forgeable by hand-editing a JSON status field, which is the guards most safety-critical property (plan.md standing rule 4: unbacked states are the actual threat model). Fix: append the D-row half to the label, e.g. "...and must keep refusing every UNBACKED withdrawal (missing/dangling/mismatched decisionRef, or a decision overwritten to rejected/userConfirmed:false) so the mechanism cannot be forged by hand-editing JSON."
findings.resolvedReason: lattice.config.json:152 label rewritten to state three explicit clauses instead of two: (1) both gates keep EXCLUDING a decision-authorized item withdrawal, (2) both keep biting on everything NOT withdrawn (now naming the shared-alias case), (3) both keep REFUSING every UNBACKED withdrawal - no decisionRef, dangling decisionRef, decisionRef naming a real decision that does not list the item, or a decision overwritten to rejected/userConfirmed=false - with an explicit sentence that clause 3 is the safety-critical one because without it the mechanism is forgeable by hand-editing a JSON status field. This mirrors the artifact's own GREEN verdict text, which is three clauses. Verified: python3 json.loads reparses lattice.config.json, the entry is still found in validate.commands with args unchanged, and the file stays pure ASCII with zero \u escapes (it had none before). git diff is a single-line label change.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/validate-channel.ts:237-241 docstring above checkDispatchEvidence/DispatchEvidenceIssue still reads "Each CHK-xxx must have evidence: dispatch event OR subagent_result event... CHKs declaring **Owner**: main-agent in plan.md are exempt" -- an exhaustive-sounding two-way rule (evidence OR owner-exempt). This story added a third, structurally distinct exemption (decision-backed withdrawn items, its own withdrawnItems bucket, checked FIRST in the loop at line ~344) but did not update this pre-existing docstring to mention it. A future reader who only reads the function-level comment (the natural first stop before reading the body) will not learn that withdrawn items are excluded, and could mistake a withdrawn items absence-from-Covered as an unexplained gap. Not touched by CHK-002/003s scope note (which discloses core/verification.ts:212 as knowingly out of scope) -- this is the *in-scope* function whose own doc comment was left stale. Low severity since the code and rendering are correct; only the doc-comment enumeration is incomplete.
findings.resolvedReason: packages/main/src/handlers/validate-channel.ts docstring above checkDispatchEvidence/DispatchEvidenceIssue no longer enumerates an exhaustive-sounding two-way rule. It now lists THREE disjoint ways an item leaves the loop without becoming an issue, in the order the loop actually tests them: (1) WITHDRAWN, (2) OWNER-EXEMPT via plan.md, (3) EVIDENCED via dispatch/subagent_result. The withdrawn bullet states WHY it is safe in the terms the reviewer asked for: membership in withdrawnChecklistItemIdsFrom(scopeShrinkageDecision), which reads only the decision record (confirmed + userConfirmed) and never a checklist item, so an item hand-edited to a withdrawn-looking status is not in the set and is still refused - explicitly NOT an item.status string. It also records that the check is first so an authorized withdrawal is never laundered into exemptedItems or evidencedItems, matching the inline comment at the loop. Comment-only change; verified by npm --prefix packages/main run build succeeding.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts:1672-1682 withdrawnItemIntentRefs subtracts any ref also owned by a surviving item (survivingRefs built at line 1677, guard at line 1680). This is unprompted defensive logic (not requested by any CHK-002/003/004 checklist item): it stops an alias collision (two items sharing the same authored verificationIntent.id) from letting a withdrawn item's ref subtraction also remove a surviving item's genuinely-required intent. Verified correct by inspection (plain set-difference; positional refs are inherently per-item since they embed item.id, so only the freeform intent.id alias form can collide) but there is zero test coverage for it: grepping the whole repo (packages/main/tests, packages/main/src/tasks) for withdrawnItemIntentRefs/survivingRefs finds only the definition site in proofstory.ts itself. A future edit that inverts or drops this guard would silently exempt a surviving item's required intent from evaluateReviewCompleteness (a real gate-relaxation bug, not just cosmetic) with no red test catching the regression. Worth a dedicated fixture (two items, one withdrawn, sharing one authored intent.id) rather than relying on code review to keep it correct.
findings.resolvedReason: Added two rows to packages/main/tests/red/red-b45a5-withdrawal-gates.mjs plus a new buildAliasCollision() fixture. C9 (premise, CONTROL-OK) measures that the collision is real: a withdrawn item CHK-002 and a SURVIVING item CHK-003 both author intent id INT-SHARED-ALIAS, an in-force binding AB-003 demands that alias for the surviving item, the helper resolves the withdrawal to CHK-002 only, and the exclusion is live in this very fixture (the withdrawn item's exclusive positional ref CHK-002:happy:0 is no longer demanded) - so E1 can never be satisfied by the subtraction simply not running. E1 (REFUSED) measures the surviving item: all refs it owns, alias included, must still be demanded by both gates. VERIFIED TO BITE BY ABLATION, not by assertion: removed the survivingRefs subtraction from packages/main/dist/core/proofstory.js withdrawnItemIntentRefs, re-ran, and E1 moved REFUSED -> PARTIAL with exit 1 and B45A5-VERDICT=BYPASS, while a sorted diff of every B45A5-ROW/VERDICT marker shows E1 and VERDICT are the ONLY two that move - all ten earlier controls stay CONTROL-OK, B1/B2/B3 stay GREEN, all seven D rows stay REFUSED, confirming no pre-existing row covered this. dist then restored from backup and verified byte-exact with shasum -a 256 -c (ed16fdb72cf50c1f0290d0bb8e6e8011bc980bbb8d04dc5d2e2bb512f2380a1d, OK). PARTIAL not BYPASSED because checkDispatchEvidence keys on item id and never reads an intent ref, so an alias collision cannot structurally reach it; the header records that honestly and explains why the channel conjunct is kept anyway. PARTIAL is a failing verdict exactly as for a D row. SELECTOR RULE: both new ids carry values designed to stay (C9=CONTROL-OK, E1=REFUSED); no existing pin changed value. Artifact still exits 0 in default mode and 0 in --attest.
